thread.title: Apple Stock Could Rise Because Weak iPhone Sales Are 'Baked In'

author: Barron's
title: Apple Stock Could Rise Because Weak iPhone Sales Are 'Baked In'
text:
Photograph by Daniel Acker/Bloomberg Weaker demand for the latest iPhones is now priced into Apple 's stock, according to Piper Jaffray.
The firm's analyst Michael Olson lowered his price target for Apple stock to $222 from $250, but he reiterated his Overweight rating for the shares. He cited positive results from its annual survey of U.S. iPhone users.
"Given the solid U.S. demand observed in our survey, weaker iPhone-component-supplier results must be due to slower int'l uptake," he wrote on Thursday. "Regarding AAPL shares, we believe int'l iPhone weakness and disappointment around lack of future unit disclosure are both largely baked into the stock."
Apple stock was up 1.7% to $171.89 on Thursday. Olson's reduced price target implies upside of more than 29%.

The company's shares have declined more than 20% since the end of October as concerns have mounted about weak demand for the newest iPhone models, amid guidance warnings from several component suppliers.
https://asset.barrons.com/dj-mg/dice/barrons-staffpicks-2d590600-c862-4394-b9d3-66b48c376d60/inset.json
Last month, The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Apple cut orders for all three newly released iPhone models.
But the Olson said Piper Jaffray's survey of more than 550 U.S. iPhone users revealed upgrade rates for the latest iPhone models was slightly better than 2017's survey levels.
Olson also noted that Apple's current valuation of 12 times forward earnings was below its two-year average of 15 times.
"We believe a price target multiple that is a slight premium to the 2-yr historical average is reasonable due to a large and entrenched base of active Apple device users," he wrote.
